faqSecurityAnswer: Yes! Qython uses advanced encryption — TLS 1.3 for data in transit and AES-256 for data at rest — and is fully compliant with GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation). Your data is stored securely on servers protected with multiple layers of security.
faqTrialAnswer: Absolutely! We offer a 14-day free trial with full access to all features. No credit card required to start.
faqCancelQuestion: Can I cancel at any time?
faqCancelAnswer: Yes! There are no contracts or penalties. You can cancel your subscription at any time directly from the settings panel.
faqIntegrationQuestion: Can I use my own study materials?
faqIntegrationAnswer: Yes! The Smart Library allows you to upload PDFs (books, articles, guidelines) and Qython's AI will use these documents as references in responses, automatically citing sources. It's perfect for customizing the AI's knowledge with your favorite materials.
faqAccuracyQuestion: How does Qython's medical AI work?
faqAccuracyAnswer: Qython uses advanced artificial intelligence trained with over 10,000 scientific articles, medical literature, and constantly updated clinical guidelines. The AI acts as an evidence-based clinical decision support tool, assisting in differential clinical reasoning and suggesting complementary investigations. Important: AI is a support tool, it does not replace professional medical judgment.
faqTrainingQuestion: Do I need training to use it?
faqTrainingAnswer: No! Qython was designed to be intuitive. Most users start using it productively in less than 5 minutes. Additionally, we offer video tutorials and dedicated support.
faqOfflineAnswer: Yes, partially. You can access already saved consultations and make offline notes. Features that depend on AI (such as diagnoses and summaries) require internet connection.
faqDataImportQuestion: Can I import my old data?
faqDataImportAnswer: Yes! We accept data import in CSV, Excel, and PDF formats. Our support team can assist with the data migration process from your previous system.
faqPrivacyQuestion: Who has access to my patient data?
faqPrivacyAnswer: Your data is protected by strict access controls and advanced encryption. Only you have access to your consultations, prescriptions, and materials. Our team's access is restricted, audited, and limited to what is strictly necessary for system maintenance and support.
faqSpecialtiesQuestion: Does Qython work for all specialties?
faqSpecialtiesAnswer: Yes! We have optimized templates for over 20 medical specialties, including Cardiology, Neurology, Pediatrics, Gynecology, Orthopedics, and many others.
faqTechRequirementsAnswer: No! Qython is entirely web-based. Just a modern browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge) and internet connection. Works on Windows, Mac, Linux, tablets, and smartphones.
faqUsageLimitsAnswer: In the Pro plan, there are no limits on consultations or AI usage. In the Basic plan, you have a generous limit of 100 consultations/month and 50 AI interactions/day.
faqAnnualDiscountQuestion: Is there a discount for annual payment?
faqAnnualDiscountAnswer: Yes! When choosing the annual plan, you save 20% compared to monthly payment. That's 2 free months per year!
faqDracmasAnswer: Dracmas is our virtual currency used for premium resources like podcast generation, video lessons, and custom simulations. Pro subscribers receive 10,000 Dracmas monthly bonus.

privacySection2Content:
We collect the following categories of data:

**2.1 Personal Registration Data:**
• Full name
• Email address
• Phone number
• Occupation (doctor, medical student, etc.)
• Professional identifier (CRM, CPF or equivalent)
• University and period (for students)
• Country of residence

**2.2 Usage Data:**
• Medical document templates created by you
• History of generated consultations (anamneses, evolutions, prescriptions)
• Platform usage logs (date/time, functionalities used)
• Payment data (processed by dLocal - we do not store cards)

**2.3 Technical Data:**
• IP address
• Browser type and device
• Operating system
• Technical and analytical cookies

**2.4 Prescription Data:**
• Prescribed medications, dosage, frequency and duration
• Patient name (as provided by the prescribing doctor)
• Prescription type and clinical notes
• History of generated prescriptions

**2.5 Visitor Data (Non-Users):**
When patients or third parties access public prescription pages shared via QR code:
• Geolocation (only with explicit consent, to locate nearby pharmacies)
• Basic technical data (IP, browser, device)
• Prescription view count

**IMPORTANT:** Prescription data is securely stored and accessible only to the prescribing doctor and, when shared via QR code, to the link holder. Qython recommends that doctors do not enter identifiable data beyond what is necessary for the prescription. The use of identifiable patient data beyond the scope of the prescription violates our Terms of Use.
privacySection3Content:
We process your personal data based on the following legal bases:

• **Contract Execution** (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR / Art. 7(V) LGPD): To provide the Service and process payments.
• **Consent** (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR / Art. 7(I) LGPD): For marketing communications (you may revoke at any time).
• **Legitimate Interest** (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR / Art. 7(IX) LGPD): To improve our AI algorithms using anonymized and aggregated data, fraud prevention, and security.
• **Legal Obligation** (Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR / Art. 7(II) LGPD): To comply with fiscal and legal obligations.
privacySection4Content:

• Provide, operate and maintain the Service
• Process payments and manage your account
• Improve our artificial intelligence algorithms (using anonymized and aggregated data)
• Send important service updates

• Comply with legal and regulatory obligations
• Send marketing communications (only with your opt-in consent, you can cancel at any time)

**Minimal access (drive.file scope):** we request only Google's *drive.file* scope, which grants access solely to files that Qython creates or that you explicitly select to import. Qython cannot see, read, or modify the other files in your Google Drive.

**Your files stay with you:** the documents you add to the Library are stored in your own cloud account, inside a dedicated folder ("Qython"). After processing, Qython does not retain the original file on its servers.

**What we keep:** to operate the Smart Library, we store only data derived from processing — extracted text, vector representations (embeddings), and thumbnails — needed for search, chat, and material generation. This data resides on our servers and is not shared with third parties.

**Credentials:** the refresh token that authorizes access to your cloud is stored encrypted at rest. We never request or store your cloud account password.

**Revoke at any time:** you can disconnect your cloud in Qython's settings or revoke access directly in your Google Account at myaccount.google.com/permissions. Disconnecting immediately ends Qython's access to your files.

**Limited Use:** Qython's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy (developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy), including the Limited Use requirements. We do not use your Drive data for advertising and do not transfer it to third parties except as necessary to provide the functionality you requested, to comply with a legal obligation, or in connection with a merger or acquisition.

interactions.amiodaroneLidocaine: Additive risk of cardiac toxicity. Avoid concurrent use.

drugs.epinephrineIVNotes: Use 1:10,000 dilution for IV. Do not mix with bicarbonate.
drugs.amiodaroneNotes: Indicated in refractory VF/VT. Dilute in 20mL D5W.
drugs.atropineNotes: Min dose 0.5mg. Ineffective in 2nd/3rd degree AV block.
drugs.ephedrineNotes: Fast-acting vasopressor. Tachyphylaxis after repeated doses.
drugs.norepinephrineNotes: Continuous infusion: 0.1-2 mcg/kg/min. Titrate to MAP. Central line preferred.
drugs.epinephrineIMNotes: IM in anterolateral thigh. Use 1:1,000. Do NOT give IV for anaphylaxis.
drugs.hydrocortisoneNotes: Adjunct — does not replace epinephrine. Effect in 4-6h.
drugs.diphenhydramineNotes: H1 antihistamine. Adjunct only, does not treat hypotension.
drugs.adenosineNotes: Rapid IV push followed by 20mL NS flush. Half-life < 10s.
drugs.calciumGluconateNotes: Infuse over 2-5 min. Monitor ECG. Indicated in hyperkalemia with ECG changes.
drugs.sodiumBicarbonateNotes: Indicated in severe metabolic acidosis (pH < 7.1). Do not mix with calcium.
drugs.magnesiumSulfateNotes: Infuse over 15-20 min. Indicated in Torsades de Pointes.
drugs.naloxoneNotes: Opioid reversal agent. Short half-life — monitor for re-sedation.
drugs.flumazenilNotes: Benzodiazepine reversal. CONTRAINDICATED in chronic BZD use and TBI.
drugs.sugammadexNotes: Reversal of rocuronium/vecuronium. 16mg/kg for immediate reversal.
drugs.ketamineNotes: RSI induction: 1-2 mg/kg IV. Maintains respiratory drive.
drugs.succinylcholineNotes: Depolarizing NMB for RSI. Onset 45-60s, duration 6-10 min.
drugs.rocuroniumRSINotes: Non-depolarizing NMB high-dose RSI. Onset 60s. Reversible with sugammadex.

acls.name: ACLS — Cardiac Arrest
acls.description: Advanced cardiovascular life support for cardiac arrest
acls.step3a: IO if IV not available within 60s
acls.step4a: VF/VT: after 2nd shock — 1mg IV every 3-5 min
acls.step5a: ETT or supraglottic device. Ventilation every 6s.
acls.step7b: Tension pneumothorax, Tamponade, Toxins, Thrombosis (PE), Thrombosis (coronary)

anaphylaxis.name: Anaphylaxis
anaphylaxis.step1a: Stop infusion, remove needle, remove allergen
anaphylaxis.step3a: Supine with legs elevated. If dyspnea: semi-upright.

mh.name: Malignant Hyperthermia
mh.description: Anesthetic emergency — hypermetabolic reaction to volatile anesthetics/succinylcholine
mh.step1a: Stop ALL halogenated agents and succinylcholine immediately
mh.step2a: Activate emergency team. Locate Dantrolene NOW.
mh.step3b: Repeat until controlled (max ~10 mg/kg or more if needed)
mh.step4b: Ice packs to axillae, groin, neck
mh.step6a: Sodium bicarbonate 1-2 mEq/kg IV per ABG
mh.step7a: Serial ABG, K+, CK, myoglobin, coagulation
mh.step8a: Dantrolene 1mg/kg IV every 4-6h for 24-48h. Monitor CK every 6h.

airway.name: Difficult Airway
airway.step5b: Do NOT delay — proceed to surgical airway
airway.step6a: Scalpel — vertical skin, horizontal through cricothyroid membrane
airway.step6b: Bougie through incision → 6.0 tube over bougie

sepsis.name: Severe Sepsis / Septic Shock
sepsis.description: Hour-1 bundle for sepsis and septic shock
sepsis.step1a: Obtain ABG. Re-measure if lactate > 2 mmol/L.
sepsis.step4a: Crystalloid 30 mL/kg within first 3h if hypotension or lactate ≥ 4
